svg.text: Glint Chat: RM ↔ customer real-time architecture
Web/mobile MFE → WebSocket gateway pods → chat-service → Artemis / AMQ, with MariaDB as the source of truth
picks a gateway pod ONCE, when the socket connects. It does not route messages.
target: ONE active relay via leader lock (D8, not built)
TTL ~30 s, refreshed by a heartbeat (~10 s)
Used for targeted routing and online / offline status.
A hint only: no entry = unknown, then broadcast.
gateways write presence on connect; the relay reads it before publishing
MULTICAST only · full-policy FAIL · message TTL 60 s
durable, one shared queue for all replicas
sends a content-free push to devices
FCM / APNs (mocked by fake-push in the lab)
push wakes the mobile app; on reconnect the app fetches missed messages from MariaDB (afterSeq)
One message, step by step (customer → RM)
A client opens a WebSocket; the load balancer picks a gateway pod once.
The gateway calls chat-service REST with the authenticated userId and the
socket's originSessionId. It never publishes chat events itself.
One DB transaction: lock the conversation row, seq = last_seq + 1, insert
message and outbox row. A resend with the same clientMsgId returns the
original ids. The origin socket gets only an ack (state SENT).
The relay polls unpublished outbox rows in id order (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED).
After commit the relay publishes to the ADDRESS chat.events, then marks
published_at. A crash in between means a duplicate, never a loss.
The broker copies the event into every bound pod queue.
Each pod writes the full message to the local sockets of every participant,
except the origin socket. Pods without such a socket do nothing.
Offline devices get a content-free push; clients resync from MariaDB by seq.
• MariaDB is the truth; the broker only carries events.
• Delivery is at-least-once: clients dedupe by messageId
• Queues are per pod, never per user (50K users, ~4 pods).
• The gateway never publishes; only the relay does, so
nothing is delivered that was not committed.
• Live delivery is an optimisation; history fetch is the net.
